The account camera grid’s render path is date-agnostic: any warranty_until value is rendered using the base neutral `chip` class. Warning/error color is only introduced by modifier classes, and no such modifier is applied to warranties. Although the seeded UI dates are future dates, the delivered rendering logic directly covers past dates without branching, so the expired-warranty outcome is deterministically neutral.

The criterion is specifically about packages named in the runtime dependency block of the delivered app manifest. Direct inspection of the complete package.json establishes the exhaustive dependency set, and every listed package is permitted by the rule; none represents a second datastore, object store, cache, queue, or third-party mail-vendor SDK.

The main commerce path largely uses integer minor units and integer-truncated tax, and the observed checkout totals are consistent with that design. However, R22 is categorical and its evaluation rule says No if any money schema field is decimal or if formatted currency is parsed. The delivered source contains both a NUMERIC(12,2) invoice-amount column and a browser money helper that parses formatted strings through Number and floating-point multiplication, so the criterion is not satisfied.

The criterion explicitly evaluates this as No when two or more handlers decode the token independently or write their own ownership filters inline. Both counterexamples are present: Astro middleware and the Hono API independently resolve bearer tokens, and several page/API handlers implement customer ownership filters/comparisons inline. A new account handler could therefore omit an ownership check without a shared abstraction catching it.

The delivered source centralizes all pinned fixture rows in one seeding routine, and each insert path either upserts on a schema-enforced unique key or is protected by an existence check. Thus running the routine a second time adds no fixture row, while no separate migration or second seed implementation also writes the fixture catalogue, devices, releases, or firmware.

The positive requirement is false. The database client reads a required value directly from the environment outside the configuration module, two required payment credential variable names are not implemented at all, and server/Astro application code contains direct environment reads plus literal hosts/ports outside the configuration module. Each is independently disqualifying under the stated evaluation rule.

The required ordered constant exists and the render paths centralize normalization through the releases library, but the seed—which writes the release notes—does not reference that constant and instead repeats the labels. The evaluation rule explicitly says this duplication is a No, so R26 is not satisfied.
